name: General Knowledge Night One — Print and Play Trivia Show

description: A ready-to-run general knowledge trivia show: five rounds, 50 questions, a tiebreaker, and every sheet you need. Print and play — no projector, no PowerPoint, no prep.
body:
The Opener — the first night in the set and the gentlest — built to get a brand-new room playing without scaring anyone off.

Five rounds, 50 questions and a tiebreaker, written to run about two hours with a break. Everything is on paper: print it, read it out, mark the sheets.

The rounds:

  • Warm-Up
  • Around the World
  • At the Movies
  • Moments in History
  • True or False

What's included:

  • Host packet — every question in running order, with the answers.
  • Team answer sheets — one per round, ready to photocopy.
  • Score sheet — room for up to 12 teams.
  • Tiebreaker — a closest-wins question for when two tables finish level.

One round is worth double, so a team that starts slow can still win it — which keeps the room in it to the end.

No screen, no projector and no software. If you can print, you can host it.

name: Classroom Trivia: Math — Print and Play, Grades 5–8
title: Classroom Trivia Math - Printable Grades 5-8 Review Game, 50 Questions
description: A ready-to-run Math review game for grades 5–8: five rounds, 50 questions and a tiebreaker. Print and play — no screen, no prep, no marking scheme to write.
body:
A full period of Math review that a class will actually play — arithmetic, shapes, measurement and the fractions-decimals-percents unit every class grinds through.

Five rounds, 50 questions and a tiebreaker. Run it as one lesson, or pull a single ten-question round as a Friday warm-up or an end-of-unit review. Everything is read aloud and answered on paper, so no projector, no devices and no textbook.

The rounds:

  • Numbers and Operations
  • Shapes and Geometry
  • Measurement and Time
  • Fractions, Decimals and Percents
  • True or False

What's included:

  • Teacher packet — every question in order, with the answers.
  • Team answer sheets — one per round, ready to photocopy.
  • Score sheet — room for up to 12 teams.
  • Tiebreaker — a closest-wins question for when two teams finish level.

The first two rounds are pitched easier and the later ones harder, so the class ramps rather than losing half the room in round one. Round four is worth double, which keeps a slow-starting team in it to the end.

Answers are written to be marked by a student swapping sheets with a neighbour: short, specific, and with the common near-miss noted where one should score.

Licensing. This price covers one teacher's own classroom — print and photocopy it for your students as often as you like. A school-wide licence, covering every teacher in the building, is $22.00 and is chosen at checkout.
